Refit a gcTMB model with other components

Source: R/refit.R
refit.Rd

refit fits a model again with some of its components changed, e.g. a new fform, rform, correlation, variance, model or family: the call of the original fit with the arguments in ... changed and all its other arguments reused (the formula, the data, the other structures, start, fix, control, ...). The new fit is a fit like any other, e.g. to compare with the original by anova.gcTMB or AIC. To change the parameters of a fit without fitting it again, e.g. for the true model of a simulation, use update.gcTMB.

Usage

refit(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
refit(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gcTMB'
refit(object, ..., startfrom = c("data", "fit"))

Arguments

object

A gcTMB object, the result of gcTMB.

...

The arguments of gcTMB to change, named, e.g. fform=b1 + b2 ~ trt, correlation=corCAR1(form=~ DAS | Plant_ID) or model="gompertz"; NULL removes a component, e.g. correlation=NULL. An unnamed first argument changes the formula, as update.formula. For other objects, the arguments of the refit method of lme4.

startfrom

Character string. The starting values: "data" (default) for those of gcTMBstart, or "fit" for the estimates of object where they carry over, see Details.

Value

A gcTMB object.

Details

The starting values of the new fit are chosen by startfrom:

  • "data" (default): from the data, as for a new call of gcTMB (see gcTMBstart);

  • "fit": from the estimates of the fit being refitted, where they carry over, as a start list (see gcTMB): the coefficients with the same name, growth model and link (e.g. the intercepts when covariates are added to fform, or all coefficients when only the correlation, the variance function or the random effects change); the variances and covariances of the random effects of the parameters on the same grouping factor (e.g. that of b1 when b2 is added to b1 ~ 1 | Plant_ID); the residual standard deviation or dispersion with the same family and variance function; and the parameters of the correlation structure and of the variance function when the refit keeps them (and they are not fixed). The rest starts from the data, e.g. the new coefficients of covariates, all coefficients of a new growth model, and the correlations of a random effect with a new one. With a new rform, the residual standard deviation of the fit may not suit the new random effects, but the optimiser moves it with them. A start, correlation or variance given in ... is used as given. The call of the new fit shows the starting values used.

The data are found again by their name in the call, so a data frame changed since the original fit gives a fit to the changed data.

The package lme4 has a refit function of its own, for a fit to a new response. For objects that are not gcTMB fits, refit calls that of lme4; if lme4 is attached after gcTMB, its refit masks this one, and gcTMB::refit refits a gcTMB model.

See also

update.gcTMB to set the parameters of a fit without refitting it.

Examples

fit <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, rform=b1 + b2 ~ 1 | Plant_ID, data=FabaHeights25)
# another growth model, and covariates on b1 and b2, the other arguments reused
fitg <- refit(fit, model="gompertz")
FabaHeights25$trt <- factor(FabaHeights25$Treatment)
fitt <- refit(fit, fform=b1 + b2 ~ trt)
anova(fit, fitt)
#> Likelihood ratio tests of gcTMB models
#> 
#>      npar    AIC    BIC  logLik deviance     LR Df Pr(>LR)
#> fit     7 1041.3 1064.4 -513.67   1027.3                  
#> fitt   15 1046.3 1095.8 -508.17   1016.3 11.006  8  0.2014
# an autocorrelation structure with a random asymptote only
fitc <- refit(fit, rform=b1 ~ 1 | Plant_ID, correlation=corCAR1(form=~ DAS | Plant_ID))
# a refit that starts from the estimates of the fit it refits
fitc2 <- refit(fitc, fform=b1 + b2 ~ trt, startfrom="fit")
fitc2$call
#> gcTMB(form = Height ~ DAS, fform = b1 + b2 ~ trt, rform = b1 ~ 
#>     1 | Plant_ID, data = FabaHeights25, start = list(fixef = c(121.07040092474, 
#> NA, NA, NA, NA, 30.6368811016357, NA, NA, NA, NA, 12.9877198644004, 
#> 0, 1), VarCorr = list(Plant_ID = 106.828045118857), sigma = 4.30919732396573), 
#>     correlation = corCAR1(value = 0.97266882677351, form = ~DAS | 
#>         Plant_ID))
